topic: Hepatitis C pangenotypic DAAs (glecaprevir/pibrentasvir, sof/vel)
front: Treatment-naive HCV, no cirrhosis. Pangenotypic options and must-do screens?
bottom: Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir 8 weeks or sofosbuvir/velpatasvir 12 weeks.

bullets.clue: Screen for HBV first: DAAs carry a boxed warning for HBV reactivation.
bullets.treat: Check DDIs: acid suppressants lower velpatasvir; rifampin is contraindicated.
bullets.trap: Sofosbuvir plus amiodarone can cause serious bradycardia.

back: Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir 8 weeks or sofosbuvir/velpatasvir 12 weeks. Key clue: Screen for HBV first: DAAs carry a boxed warning for HBV reactivation. Pharmacist move: Check DDIs: acid suppressants lower velpatasvir; rifampin is contraindicated. Exam trap: Sofosbuvir plus amiodarone can cause serious bradycardia.

source.recommendation: AASLD/IDSA HCV Guidance (2026): simplified treatment of treatment-naive adults without cirrhosis—glecaprevir/pibrentasvir × 8 weeks or sofosbuvir/velpatasvir × 12 weeks; test HBsAg/anti-HBc before treatment; assess DDIs. Labeling: boxed warning for HBV reactivation; serious symptomatic bradycardia with amiodarone and sofosbuvir; PPIs/H2RAs reduce velpatasvir exposure.

topic: CKD: SGLT2i/finerenone, dose adjustments, anemia/ESA
front: T2D with CKD, eGFR 35, albuminuria. Which kidney-protective drugs, and metformin?
bottom: SGLT2i (eGFR ≥20) and RASi; consider finerenone.

bullets.clue: Finerenone: T2D with albuminuria, eGFR ≥25, normal potassium.
bullets.treat: Metformin: reduce dose below eGFR 45; stop below 30.
bullets.trap: Treat iron deficiency before an ESA; don't target normal hemoglobin.

back: SGLT2i (eGFR ≥20) and RASi; consider finerenone. Key clue: Finerenone: T2D with albuminuria, eGFR ≥25, normal potassium. Pharmacist move: Metformin: reduce dose below eGFR 45; stop below 30. Exam trap: Treat iron deficiency before an ESA; don't target normal hemoglobin.

source.guideline: KDIGO 2024 CKD; KDIGO 2022 Diabetes in CKD
source.recommendation: KDIGO 2024 CKD: SGLT2i for CKD with eGFR ≥20; RASi for albuminuria; KDIGO 2022 Diabetes in CKD: ns-MRA (finerenone) for T2D with eGFR ≥25, normal potassium and albuminuria ≥30 mg/g despite RASi; metformin reduce dose eGFR 30–44, stop <30. KDIGO anemia: correct iron deficiency before ESA; avoid targeting normal hemoglobin.

topic: Nephrotoxins and AKI drug management
front: AKI on day 3 in a patient on ibuprofen, lisinopril and gentamicin. Pharmacist actions?
bottom: Stop nephrotoxins and re-dose by current kidney function.

bullets.clue: Stop the NSAID; hold the ACEi and other nephrotoxins while kidney function is unstable.
bullets.treat: Avoid aminoglycosides when alternatives exist; use isotonic crystalloid, not colloids.
bullets.trap: Loop diuretics don't treat AKI; use only for volume overload.

back: Stop nephrotoxins and re-dose by current kidney function. Key clue: Stop the NSAID; hold the ACEi and other nephrotoxins while kidney function is unstable. Pharmacist move: Avoid aminoglycosides when alternatives exist; use isotonic crystalloid, not colloids. Exam trap: Loop diuretics don't treat AKI; use only for volume overload.

source.guideline: KDIGO 2012 AKI (2026 AKI/AKD guideline in final prep; public draft Mar 2026)
source.recommendation: KDIGO 2012 AKI guideline: discontinue nephrotoxic agents when possible; avoid aminoglycosides unless no suitable alternative; isotonic crystalloids rather than colloids for volume expansion; do not use diuretics to treat AKI except for volume overload; adjust drug dosing to kidney function.

recheck_note: KDIGO 2012 AKI is still the current final guideline, but the 2026 KDIGO AKI/AKD update was a public draft (Mar 2026). Recheck kdigo.org for the final version before publishing.

topic: Hyponatremia correction limits (≤8–10 mEq/L/day)
front: Chronic hyponatremia, Na 112, alcohol use disorder. Max correction in 24 hours?
bottom: ≤8 mEq/L in 24 hours: high risk of demyelination.

bullets.clue: Usual limit 10–12 mEq/L in 24 h; ≤8 with alcoholism, malnutrition, hypokalemia, liver disease.
bullets.treat: Severe symptoms: 3% saline 100 mL bolus, may repeat.
bullets.trap: Overcorrection: re-lower with D5W and desmopressin.

back: ≤8 mEq/L in 24 hours: high risk of demyelination. Key clue: Usual limit 10–12 mEq/L in 24 h; ≤8 with alcoholism, malnutrition, hypokalemia, liver disease. Pharmacist move: Severe symptoms: 3% saline 100 mL bolus, may repeat. Exam trap: Overcorrection: re-lower with D5W and desmopressin.

diagram.alt: Chronic hyponatremia correction limits: usual 10 to 12 mEq/L per 24 hours; 8 or less in high osmotic demyelination risk (sodium 105 or less, alcohol use disorder, malnutrition, hypokalemia, liver disease). Severe symptoms: 3 percent saline 100 mL bolus. Overcorrection: D5W with or without desmopressin.

source.recommendation: US Expert Panel 2013 hyponatremia recommendations: chronic hyponatremia correction limit 10–12 mmol/L in 24 h (8 mmol/L in 24 h for high ODS risk: Na ≤105, hypokalemia, alcoholism, malnutrition, liver disease); 3% saline 100 mL bolus for severe symptoms; manage overcorrection with D5W ± desmopressin.

topic: Gout: allopurinol treat-to-target <6, flare therapy, colchicine dosing
front: Recurrent gout, starting allopurinol. Dose, goal and flare protection?
bottom: Start ≤100 mg daily; titrate to urate <6 mg/dL.

bullets.clue: Start lower (e.g., 50 mg) in CKD stage 3+; HLA-B*5801 test in Southeast Asian and African American patients.
bullets.treat: Flare prophylaxis (e.g., colchicine) for 3–6 months; keep ULT during flares.
bullets.trap: Flare colchicine: 1.2 mg, then 0.6 mg 1 hour later.

back: Start ≤100 mg daily; titrate to urate <6 mg/dL. Key clue: Start lower (e.g., 50 mg) in CKD stage 3+; HLA-B*5801 test in Southeast Asian and African American patients. Pharmacist move: Flare prophylaxis (e.g., colchicine) for 3–6 months; keep ULT during flares. Exam trap: Flare colchicine: 1.2 mg, then 0.6 mg 1 hour later.

source.recommendation: ACR 2020 gout: allopurinol first-line, start ≤100 mg/day (lower in CKD ≥3), treat to serum urate <6 mg/dL; HLA-B*5801 testing in Southeast Asian and African American patients; anti-inflammatory prophylaxis 3–6 months; continue ULT during flares; low-dose colchicine for flares (1.2 mg then 0.6 mg 1 h later).

topic: RA: methotrexate first-line, folic acid, biologic screening (TB/HBV)
front: New RA on methotrexate. Dosing, supplement, and pre-biologic screening?
bottom: Once weekly, plus folic acid.

bullets.clue: Methotrexate is first-line, titrated to ~25 mg weekly as tolerated.
bullets.treat: Before biologics or JAK inhibitors: screen for TB and hepatitis B and C.
bullets.trap: Daily dosing errors are fatal: stress 'weekly.'

back: Once weekly, plus folic acid. Key clue: Methotrexate is first-line, titrated to ~25 mg weekly as tolerated. Pharmacist move: Before biologics or JAK inhibitors: screen for TB and hepatitis B and C. Exam trap: Daily dosing errors are fatal: stress 'weekly.'

source.recommendation: ACR 2021 RA: methotrexate monotherapy preferred initial DMARD, titrated to ≥15 mg/week within 4–6 weeks; folic acid supplementation. Biologic/tsDMARD labeling: screen for latent TB and HBV before starting; ISMP: weekly methotrexate dosing errors.

topic: Osteoarthritis: topical NSAID, acetaminophen, avoid opioids
front: Knee OA pain in a 70-year-old. First-line drug, and are opioids an option?
bottom: Topical NSAID first.

bullets.clue: Oral NSAIDs if needed, considering GI, renal and CV risk.
bullets.treat: Acetaminophen and tramadol: conditional; other opioids: conditionally against.
bullets.trap: Glucosamine, chondroitin and hydroxychloroquine aren't recommended.

back: Topical NSAID first. Key clue: Oral NSAIDs if needed, considering GI, renal and CV risk. Pharmacist move: Acetaminophen and tramadol: conditional; other opioids: conditionally against. Exam trap: Glucosamine, chondroitin and hydroxychloroquine aren't recommended.

source.recommendation: ACR/AF 2019 OA: strongly recommend topical NSAIDs for knee OA and oral NSAIDs; conditionally recommend acetaminophen and tramadol; conditionally against non-tramadol opioids; strongly against glucosamine, hydroxychloroquine, bisphosphonates; against chondroitin for knee/hip.

topic: Depression: SSRI first-line, onset, switching, discontinuation
front: Sertraline started 2 weeks ago, 'not working yet.' What do you counsel?
bottom: Full effect takes 4–8 weeks: keep taking it.

bullets.clue: Adequate trial: 4–8 weeks at a therapeutic dose.
bullets.treat: After remission, continue at least 6 months; taper to stop.
bullets.trap: Switching to an MAOI: 2-week washout, 5 weeks after fluoxetine.

back: Full effect takes 4–8 weeks: keep taking it. Key clue: Adequate trial: 4–8 weeks at a therapeutic dose. Pharmacist move: After remission, continue at least 6 months; taper to stop. Exam trap: Switching to an MAOI: 2-week washout, 5 weeks after fluoxetine.

source.recommendation: APA 2019 depression guideline: SSRIs/SNRIs among first-line options; VA/DoD MDD 2022: assess response after 4–8 weeks at adequate dose, continue ≥6 months after remission; taper to avoid discontinuation syndrome. Labeling: 14-day washout between SSRIs and MAOIs; 5 weeks after fluoxetine.

topic: Bipolar: lithium, valproate, SGAs; lamotrigine titration (SJS)
front: Bipolar patient on valproate is adding lamotrigine. How do you titrate?
bottom: Halve the usual titration: valproate doubles lamotrigine levels.

bullets.clue: Usual start: 25 mg daily for 2 weeks, then 50 mg daily for 2 weeks.
bullets.treat: Lithium: trough 0.6–1.0 mEq/L (up to 1.2) maintenance; monitor renal and thyroid.
bullets.trap: Any rash on lamotrigine: stop and seek care (SJS risk).

back: Halve the usual titration: valproate doubles lamotrigine levels. Key clue: Usual start: 25 mg daily for 2 weeks, then 50 mg daily for 2 weeks. Pharmacist move: Lithium: trough 0.6–1.0 mEq/L (up to 1.2) maintenance; monitor renal and thyroid. Exam trap: Any rash on lamotrigine: stop and seek care (SJS risk).

source.recommendation: VA/DoD Bipolar 2023: lithium, valproate, SGAs, lamotrigine (maintenance/depression). Lamotrigine labeling: boxed warning for serious rash; standard titration 25 mg/day weeks 1–2, 50 mg/day weeks 3–4; reduce dose ~50% with valproate; re-titrate if stopped >5 half-lives. Lithium labeling/CANMAT 2018: maintenance levels 0.6–1.0 mEq/L; monitor renal and thyroid function.

topic: Schizophrenia: SGA selection, clozapine for TRS, LAIs
front: Schizophrenia failed two antipsychotics. Next drug, and what monitoring stays?
bottom: Clozapine for treatment-resistant schizophrenia.

bullets.clue: The clozapine REMS ended in 2025; ANC monitoring per labeling still applies.
bullets.treat: Watch myocarditis, constipation/ileus and seizures; metabolic monitoring for all SGAs.
bullets.trap: Nonadherence: offer a long-acting injectable.

back: Clozapine for treatment-resistant schizophrenia. Key clue: The clozapine REMS ended in 2025; ANC monitoring per labeling still applies. Pharmacist move: Watch myocarditis, constipation/ileus and seizures; metabolic monitoring for all SGAs. Exam trap: Nonadherence: offer a long-acting injectable.

source.recommendation: APA 2020 schizophrenia guideline: clozapine for treatment-resistant schizophrenia; LAI antipsychotic if preferred or history of nonadherence; metabolic monitoring. FDA 2025: clozapine REMS eliminated; labeling retains neutropenia warnings and ANC monitoring; warnings for myocarditis, GI hypomotility, seizures.

topic: Anxiety & insomnia: SSRI/SNRI, buspirone, avoid benzo/Z-drug in elderly
front: A 78-year-old asks for zolpidem for sleep. Better plan?
bottom: Avoid: CBT-I first.

bullets.clue: Beers: avoid benzodiazepines and Z-drugs in older adults (falls, delirium).
bullets.treat: If a drug is needed: low-dose doxepin ≤6 mg; for anxiety, SSRI/SNRI or buspirone.
bullets.trap: Diphenhydramine is strongly anticholinergic: avoid too.

back: Avoid: CBT-I first. Key clue: Beers: avoid benzodiazepines and Z-drugs in older adults (falls, delirium). Pharmacist move: If a drug is needed: low-dose doxepin ≤6 mg; for anxiety, SSRI/SNRI or buspirone. Exam trap: Diphenhydramine is strongly anticholinergic: avoid too.

source.guideline: AASM 2017 insomnia (+AASM 2026 CBT-I + medication); AGS Beers 2023
source.recommendation: AASM 2017 pharmacologic insomnia guideline (+2026 update): CBT-I first; options include low-dose doxepin. AGS Beers 2023: avoid benzodiazepines, Z-drugs (eszopiclone, zaleplon, zolpidem) and first-generation antihistamines in older adults. Anxiety: SSRIs/SNRIs first-line, buspirone alternative.

topic: ADHD stimulants: dosing, CII rules, nonstimulants
front: ADHD, age 8, starting methylphenidate ER. Refill rules and nonstimulant options?
bottom: C-II: no refills; new prescription each time.

bullets.clue: Prescriber may issue multiple prescriptions up to a 90-day supply.
bullets.treat: Nonstimulants: atomoxetine, viloxazine, guanfacine ER, clonidine ER.
bullets.trap: Atomoxetine and viloxazine carry boxed warnings for suicidal thoughts.

back: C-II: no refills; new prescription each time. Key clue: Prescriber may issue multiple prescriptions up to a 90-day supply. Pharmacist move: Nonstimulants: atomoxetine, viloxazine, guanfacine ER, clonidine ER. Exam trap: Atomoxetine and viloxazine carry boxed warnings for suicidal thoughts.

source.recommendation: AAP 2019 ADHD: ages 6–11 FDA-approved medication plus behavioral therapy; ages 4–5 behavioral therapy first, methylphenidate if needed. 21 CFR 1306.12: no refills of Schedule II; multiple prescriptions up to 90-day supply permitted. Atomoxetine labeling: boxed warning for suicidal ideation.

topic: OUD: buprenorphine induction, methadone, naltrexone; X-waiver removed
front: Patient wants buprenorphine for OUD. Who can prescribe, and when to start?
bottom: Any DEA practitioner with Schedule III authority: no X-waiver.

bullets.clue: Start when withdrawal is clear (e.g., COWS ≥8–12) to avoid precipitated withdrawal.
bullets.treat: Naltrexone needs 7–10 days opioid-free; methadone for OUD comes only from an OTP.
bullets.trap: Too-early buprenorphine causes precipitated withdrawal.

back: Any DEA practitioner with Schedule III authority: no X-waiver. Key clue: Start when withdrawal is clear (e.g., COWS ≥8–12) to avoid precipitated withdrawal. Pharmacist move: Naltrexone needs 7–10 days opioid-free; methadone for OUD comes only from an OTP. Exam trap: Too-early buprenorphine causes precipitated withdrawal.

source.guideline: ASAM NPG 2020 focused update (latest); MAT Act 2023
source.recommendation: ASAM National Practice Guideline 2020 focused update: begin buprenorphine when objective withdrawal signs present (e.g., COWS 8–12+); naltrexone after 7–10 days opioid-free; methadone for OUD dispensed through OTPs. Consolidated Appropriations Act 2023 (MAT Act): DATA-waiver (X-waiver) eliminated; any practitioner with Schedule III DEA registration may prescribe buprenorphine for OUD.

topic: Opioid overdose: naloxone OTC, nalmefene
front: Bystander gives OTC naloxone nasal spray. Counsel the steps.
bottom: One spray in a nostril, call 911, repeat every 2–3 min if needed.

bullets.clue: Naloxone 4 mg nasal has been OTC since 2023.
bullets.treat: Use a new device in the other nostril for repeat doses; stay with the person.
bullets.trap: Naloxone can wear off before the opioid: watch for re-sedation.

back: One spray in a nostril, call 911, repeat every 2–3 min if needed. Key clue: Naloxone 4 mg nasal has been OTC since 2023. Pharmacist move: Use a new device in the other nostril for repeat doses; stay with the person. Exam trap: Naloxone can wear off before the opioid: watch for re-sedation.

source.recommendation: FDA March 2023 approved Narcan 4 mg naloxone nasal spray for OTC use; labeling: give one spray, call 911, may repeat every 2–3 minutes in alternating nostrils with a new device; effect may be shorter than opioid. CDC 2022: offer naloxone when overdose risk increased. Nalmefene (Rx) is a longer-acting alternative.

topic: Alcohol withdrawal and AUD pharmacotherapy (naltrexone, acamprosate)
front: Alcohol withdrawal now; later wants to stay sober. Drugs for each?
bottom: Withdrawal: benzodiazepine. AUD: naltrexone or acamprosate.

bullets.clue: Give thiamine before glucose.
bullets.treat: Naltrexone: no with opioids or acute hepatitis. Acamprosate: adjust for renal function; avoid CrCl ≤30.
bullets.trap: Disulfiram isn't first-line.

back: Withdrawal: benzodiazepine. AUD: naltrexone or acamprosate. Key clue: Give thiamine before glucose. Pharmacist move: Naltrexone: no with opioids or acute hepatitis. Acamprosate: adjust for renal function; avoid CrCl ≤30. Exam trap: Disulfiram isn't first-line.

source.recommendation: ASAM 2020 alcohol withdrawal: benzodiazepines first-line; phenobarbital alternative; thiamine. APA 2018 AUD: naltrexone or acamprosate first-line; disulfiram not first-line. Labeling: naltrexone contraindicated with opioid use; acamprosate dose-reduce CrCl 30–50, contraindicated CrCl ≤30.

topic: Smoking cessation: varenicline, NRT combination
front: Smoker with stable CAD wants to quit. Most effective plan and varenicline titration?
bottom: Varenicline, ideally starting a week before quit day.

bullets.clue: 0.5 mg daily ×3 days, 0.5 mg BID ×4 days, then 1 mg BID for 12 weeks.
bullets.treat: Combination NRT (patch plus gum or lozenge) beats single NRT.
bullets.trap: NRT is safe in stable cardiovascular disease.

back: Varenicline, ideally starting a week before quit day. Key clue: 0.5 mg daily ×3 days, 0.5 mg BID ×4 days, then 1 mg BID for 12 weeks. Pharmacist move: Combination NRT (patch plus gum or lozenge) beats single NRT. Exam trap: NRT is safe in stable cardiovascular disease.

source.recommendation: ACC 2018 ECDP tobacco cessation: varenicline first-line, combination NRT preferred over single NRT; NRT safe in stable CVD. USPSTF 2021: offer behavioral interventions and FDA-approved pharmacotherapy. Varenicline labeling: titration 0.5 mg daily days 1–3, 0.5 mg BID days 4–7, then 1 mg BID; boxed warning removed 2016.

topic: Status epilepticus: benzodiazepine then fosphenytoin/levetiracetam/VPA
front: Seizure lasting 6 minutes, IV access. First and second-line drugs?
bottom: Lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg IV (max 4 mg/dose), may repeat.

bullets.clue: No IV: midazolam 10 mg IM (>40 kg).
bullets.treat: Then fosphenytoin 20 mg PE/kg, levetiracetam 60 mg/kg or valproate 40 mg/kg.
bullets.trap: ESETT: second-line agents work about equally.

back: Lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg IV (max 4 mg/dose), may repeat. Key clue: No IV: midazolam 10 mg IM (>40 kg). Pharmacist move: Then fosphenytoin 20 mg PE/kg, levetiracetam 60 mg/kg or valproate 40 mg/kg. Exam trap: ESETT: second-line agents work about equally.

diagram.alt: Convulsive status epilepticus timeline: at 5 minutes a benzodiazepine (IV lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg up to 4 mg, may repeat once, or IM midazolam 10 mg if over 40 kg); at 20 minutes a second-line drug: fosphenytoin 20 mg PE/kg, levetiracetam 60 mg/kg or valproate 40 mg/kg, which work about equally.

source.guideline: AES 2016 (still current; AES update in development); NCS 2012; ESETT 2019
source.recommendation: AES 2016 convulsive status epilepticus guideline: benzodiazepine at 5 minutes (IV lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg max 4 mg/dose, IM midazolam 10 mg >40 kg, or IV diazepam); second phase fosphenytoin 20 mg PE/kg, valproate 40 mg/kg, or levetiracetam 60 mg/kg; ESETT 2019 found similar efficacy.

topic: Epilepsy: AED choice in women of childbearing potential
front: Woman of childbearing age with epilepsy. Which antiseizure drug to avoid most?
bottom: Valproate: highest risk of malformations and lower IQ.

bullets.clue: Lower risk: lamotrigine, levetiracetam, oxcarbazepine.
bullets.treat: Folic acid ≥0.4 mg daily; enzyme inducers lower hormonal contraceptive effect.
bullets.trap: Lamotrigine levels fall in pregnancy: monitor and adjust.

back: Valproate: highest risk of malformations and lower IQ. Key clue: Lower risk: lamotrigine, levetiracetam, oxcarbazepine. Pharmacist move: Folic acid ≥0.4 mg daily; enzyme inducers lower hormonal contraceptive effect. Exam trap: Lamotrigine levels fall in pregnancy: monitor and adjust.

source.recommendation: AAN/AES/SMFM 2024 practice guideline for people with epilepsy of childbearing potential: avoid valproate to minimize major congenital malformations and neurodevelopmental effects; lamotrigine, levetiracetam, oxcarbazepine lower risk; folic acid ≥0.4 mg/day; monitor lamotrigine (and levetiracetam, oxcarbazepine) levels during pregnancy; enzyme-inducing ASMs reduce hormonal contraceptive efficacy.

topic: Migraine: triptans, gepants, CGRP mAbs; triptan contraindications
front: Migraine patient with prior MI. Acute options when triptans are out?
bottom: Gepants: ubrogepant or rimegepant.

bullets.clue: Triptans are contraindicated with CAD, stroke, uncontrolled HTN, hemiplegic migraine.
bullets.treat: Lasmiditan: no driving for 8 hours; it's C-V.
bullets.trap: Triptan use ≥10 days a month risks medication-overuse headache.

back: Gepants: ubrogepant or rimegepant. Key clue: Triptans are contraindicated with CAD, stroke, uncontrolled HTN, hemiplegic migraine. Pharmacist move: Lasmiditan: no driving for 8 hours; it's C-V. Exam trap: Triptan use ≥10 days a month risks medication-overuse headache.

source.recommendation: AHS 2021 consensus statement: gepants and lasmiditan for acute treatment when triptans contraindicated or not tolerated; CGRP mAbs for prevention. Triptan labeling: contraindicated in CAD, stroke, uncontrolled hypertension, hemiplegic/basilar migraine. Lasmiditan labeling: no driving for 8 h; Schedule V.

topic: Parkinson's: carbidopa/levodopa, MAO-B, drugs that worsen PD
front: Parkinson's patient with nausea gets metoclopramide. Problem? Better choice?
bottom: Yes: it blocks dopamine. Use a non-dopamine antiemetic, e.g., ondansetron.

bullets.clue: Also avoid haloperidol and prochlorperazine; psychosis: quetiapine or pimavanserin.
bullets.treat: Carbidopa/levodopa is most effective; dopamine agonists can cause impulse control disorders.
bullets.trap: MAO-B inhibitors interact with meperidine and other serotonergic drugs.

back: Yes: it blocks dopamine. Use a non-dopamine antiemetic, e.g., ondansetron. Key clue: Also avoid haloperidol and prochlorperazine; psychosis: quetiapine or pimavanserin. Pharmacist move: Carbidopa/levodopa is most effective; dopamine agonists can cause impulse control disorders. Exam trap: MAO-B inhibitors interact with meperidine and other serotonergic drugs.

source.recommendation: AAN 2021 early Parkinson disease: levodopa preferred initial therapy for most; dopamine agonists carry impulse control disorder risk. Labeling: metoclopramide, typical antipsychotics and prochlorperazine can worsen parkinsonism; MAO-B inhibitors (selegiline, rasagiline) contraindicated with meperidine; pimavanserin indicated for PD psychosis.

topic: Acute ischemic stroke: tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg or alteplase 0.9 mg/kg ≤4.5 h, BP <185/110 before lysis
front: Ischemic stroke, last known well 2 hours ago, BP 192/104. Lytic dose and BP goal?
bottom: Lower BP to <185/110 first, then lyse.

bullets.clue: Tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg (max 25 mg) single bolus, or alteplase 0.9 mg/kg (max 90 mg).
bullets.treat: Alteplase: 10% bolus, rest over 60 minutes; keep BP <180/105 for 24 hours.
bullets.trap: Window is 4.5 hours from last known well.

back: Lower BP to <185/110 first, then lyse. Key clue: Tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg (max 25 mg) single bolus, or alteplase 0.9 mg/kg (max 90 mg). Pharmacist move: Alteplase: 10% bolus, rest over 60 minutes; keep BP <180/105 for 24 hours. Exam trap: Window is 4.5 hours from last known well.

source.recommendation: AHA/ASA 2026 acute ischemic stroke guideline: IV thrombolysis within 4.5 h with tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg (max 25 mg) or alteplase 0.9 mg/kg (max 90 mg; 10% bolus, remainder over 60 min); BP <185/110 before and <180/105 for 24 h after thrombolysis.

topic: Secondary stroke prevention: short-term DAPT after minor stroke/TIA
front: Minor stroke (NIHSS 2) 12 hours ago. Antiplatelet plan?
bottom: Aspirin + clopidogrel for 21 days, then one agent.

bullets.clue: Start within 24 hours with a clopidogrel loading dose.
bullets.treat: Alternative: ticagrelor plus aspirin for 30 days.
bullets.trap: Long-term DAPT adds bleeding without benefit.

back: Aspirin + clopidogrel for 21 days, then one agent. Key clue: Start within 24 hours with a clopidogrel loading dose. Pharmacist move: Alternative: ticagrelor plus aspirin for 30 days. Exam trap: Long-term DAPT adds bleeding without benefit.

source.recommendation: AHA/ASA 2021 secondary stroke prevention: minor ischemic stroke (NIHSS ≤3) or high-risk TIA—DAPT with aspirin and clopidogrel started within 24 h and continued 21 days (POINT/CHANCE), or ticagrelor plus aspirin for 30 days; then single antiplatelet; long-term DAPT not recommended.

topic: Alzheimer's: cholinesterase inhibitors, memantine, anti-amyloid mAbs (ARIA)
front: Early Alzheimer's starting lecanemab. Key safety monitoring?
bottom: ARIA: MRI at baseline and during titration.

bullets.clue: APOE ε4 homozygotes have the highest ARIA risk; test before starting.
bullets.treat: Mild-moderate disease: donepezil; moderate-severe: add memantine.
bullets.trap: Use caution with anticoagulants: ARIA can bleed.

back: ARIA: MRI at baseline and during titration. Key clue: APOE ε4 homozygotes have the highest ARIA risk; test before starting. Pharmacist move: Mild-moderate disease: donepezil; moderate-severe: add memantine. Exam trap: Use caution with anticoagulants: ARIA can bleed.

source.recommendation: Lecanemab and donanemab labeling (2023–24): boxed warning for ARIA; baseline MRI and scheduled MRIs during dose titration; APOE ε4 testing before starting (homozygotes highest risk); caution with antithrombotics. Cholinesterase inhibitors for mild-moderate-severe AD; memantine for moderate-severe.

topic: Oncology supportive: CINV prophylaxis by emetic risk
front: Patient starting cisplatin. Antiemetic prophylaxis?
bottom: Four drugs: NK1 antagonist + 5-HT3 antagonist + dexamethasone + olanzapine.

bullets.clue: Cisplatin is highly emetogenic.
bullets.treat: Moderate risk: 5-HT3 antagonist + dexamethasone; add NK1 for carboplatin AUC ≥4.
bullets.trap: Olanzapine can sedate: counsel on drowsiness.

back: Four drugs: NK1 antagonist + 5-HT3 antagonist + dexamethasone + olanzapine. Key clue: Cisplatin is highly emetogenic. Pharmacist move: Moderate risk: 5-HT3 antagonist + dexamethasone; add NK1 for carboplatin AUC ≥4. Exam trap: Olanzapine can sedate: counsel on drowsiness.

source.recommendation: ASCO Antiemetics 2020 (2022 focused update): high-emetic-risk (e.g., cisplatin)—NK1 receptor antagonist, 5-HT3 receptor antagonist, dexamethasone and olanzapine; carboplatin AUC ≥4—NK1 RA + 5-HT3 RA + dexamethasone; moderate risk—5-HT3 RA + dexamethasone.

topic: Oncology toxicities: anthracycline cardiotoxicity, cisplatin nephrotoxicity, MTX rescue
front: Match the toxicity to the protection: doxorubicin, cisplatin, high-dose methotrexate.
bottom: Dexrazoxane; hydration/magnesium; leucovorin.

bullets.clue: Doxorubicin cardiotoxicity rises with cumulative dose; check LVEF.
